slideDifferences.nativeText:
PHRASES
MEANING
EXAMPLE
FILL THE PINCH
To experience hardship, especially financial.
Staff, we’re beginning to feel the pinch as the dispute entered its third week.
SEE THE FIT
To consider it correct or acceptable to do something.
why did the company see fit to give you the job?
KNOCK ON WOOD
said after a confident or positive statement, to express a hope for one's good luck to continue.
I haven't been banned yet, knock on wood.
FIRE IN THE BELLY
A powerful sense of ambition or determination.
He lacks the fire in his belly necessary to seek the presidency.
HOPE AGAINST HOPE
Hope or wish for with little reason or justification.
I'm hoping against hope that someone will return my wallet.
FOOL’S PARADISE
A state of happiness based on a person's not knowing about or denying the existence of potential trouble.
They were living in a fool's paradise, refusing to accept that they were in debt.
BRASS RING
A very desirable prize, goal, or opportunity
He made his first try for the brass ring when he ran for mayor a few years ago.
GAME PLAN
A strategy worked out in advance, especially in sports, politics, or business.
If he has a game plan for winning the deal, only he understands it.
Look at the phrases and  discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?

slideDifferences.nativeText:
We are able to express ideas about things or event not likely to happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.
PHRASES
EXAMPLES
What if…
What if Jane came tonight to the party? Just picture how awkward it would be.
Imagine that / if…
Imagine you fell in front of your classmates; would you laugh at yourself?
If only…
If only you could come home these days. / If only I had more time, but I am always busy.
I wish…
I wish we didn’t feel the pinch but there’s nothing we could do. / I wish it could be different.
To Consider

We work with these phrases using the simple past tense. 
When using -what if- we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 
Could and would play a major role.

We can use the grammar presented to talk about the following function:
Functions
Examples
1
Express ideas or events not likely to be true or to happen.
What if Jill had money? Would you guys accept her in the club?

Imagine they won the competition; they would never stop talking about it.

If only she  saw the fit of the project, she could be more supportive.

I wish he came to me first so I could help him.
To consider 
There are contexts where -could- and -would- express wishes for the future. E.G I don’t like my job; I wish I could get a new one.
                   That sound is so annoying; I wish it would stop.

C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.
Achieving Your Wishes : Will Wishing Work?

Do you wish you had a better job, bigger house, more friends, better health, less worries, and greater happiness? We all engage in wishing, but should we? Should we wish for more or be satisfied with what we have? Why can't we do both? Just because we are satisfied with what we have doesn't mean we can't or shouldn't wish for more. After all, isn't self-improvement or personal-development about wishing for more?

No, there isn't anything wrong with wishing. A wish is merely the voice of our Higher Self reminding us that we have boundless potential and urging us to take advantage of it. If anything, we should wish to have, be, and do more because that's how we help to create a better world; if only we always thought that way.. It is only when we have more than we need that we can share what we have with those who have less than they need. It is only when we are healthy that we can help the sick. And it is only when we are strong that we can help the weak. As you can see, wishing plays an important role, for we either allow ourselves to become what others will make of us, or we wish to become something better.

Did you ever toss a coin into a wishing well and make a wish? What if you had your own wishing well? Aware of it or not, that's precisely what we have. We have a personal genie within us. It is our subconscious. Its sole purpose is to serve us. It serves us by regulating our heart and breathing rate, body temperature, and the flow of hormones, just to name a few of its many functions. But another major function of the subconscious is to grant our every wish! And it works tirelessly, 24/7, granting us what it believes we want.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Adapted from: https://www.rotaryeclubone.org/makeups/articles/achievingyourwishe/

texts: PHRASES
MEANING
EXAMPLE
FILL THE PINCH
To experience hardship, especially financial.
Staff, we’re beginning to feel the pinch as the dispute entered its third week.
SEE THE FIT
To consider it correct or acceptable to do something.
why did the company see fit to give you the job?
KNOCK ON WOOD
said after a confident or positive statement, to express a hope for one's good luck to continue.
I haven't been banned yet, knock on wood.
FIRE IN THE BELLY
A powerful sense of ambition or determination.
He lacks the fire in his belly necessary to seek the presidency.
HOPE AGAINST HOPE
Hope or wish for with little reason or justification.
I'm hoping against hope that someone will return my wallet.
FOOL’S PARADISE
A state of happiness based on a person's not knowing about or denying the existence of potential trouble.
They were living in a fool's paradise, refusing to accept that they were in debt.
BRASS RING
A very desirable prize, goal, or opportunity
He made his first try for the brass ring when he ran for mayor a few years ago.
GAME PLAN
A strategy worked out in advance, especially in sports, politics, or business.
If he has a game plan for winning the deal, only he understands it.
Look at the phrases and  discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?

texts: We are able to express ideas about things or event not likely to happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.
PHRASES
EXAMPLES
What if…
What if Jane came tonight to the party? Just picture how awkward it would be.
Imagine that / if…
Imagine you fell in front of your classmates; would you laugh at yourself?
If only…
If only you could come home these days. / If only I had more time, but I am always busy.
I wish…
I wish we didn’t feel the pinch but there’s nothing we could do. / I wish it could be different.

To Consider

We work with these phrases using the simple past tense. 
When using -what if- we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 
Could and would play a major role.

paragraphs.text: PHRASES
EXAMPLES
What if…
What if Jane came tonight to the party? Just picture how awkward it would be.
Imagine that / if…
Imagine you fell in front of your classmates; would you laugh at yourself?
If only…
If only you could come home these days. / If only I had more time, but I am always busy.
I wish…
I wish we didn’t feel the pinch but there’s nothing we could do. / I wish it could be different.

To Consider

We work with these phrases using the simple past tense. 
When using -what if- we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 
Could and would play a major role.

texts: We can use the grammar presented to talk about the following function:
Functions
Examples
Express ideas or events not likely to be true or to happen.

What if Jill had money? Would you guys accept her in the club?

Imagine they won the competition; they would never stop talking about it.

If only she  saw the fit of the project, she could be more supportive.

I wish he came to me first so I could help him.
To consider
There are contexts where -could- and -would- express wishes for the future. E.G I don’t like my job; I wish I could get a new one.
That sound is so annoying; I wish it would stop.

texts: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.
Achieving Your Wishes : Will Wishing Work?

Do you wish you had a better job, bigger house, more friends, better health, less worries, and greater happiness? We all engage in wishing, but should we? Should we wish for more or be satisfied with what we have? Why can't we do both? Just because we are satisfied with what we have doesn't mean we can't or shouldn't wish for more. After all, isn't self-improvement or personal-development about wishing for more?

No, there isn't anything wrong with wishing. A wish is merely the voice of our Higher Self reminding us that we have boundless potential and urging us to take advantage of it. If anything, we should wish to have, be, and do more because that's how we help to create a better world; if only we always thought that way.. It is only when we have more than we need that we can share what we have with those who have less than they need. It is only when we are healthy that we can help the sick. And it is only when we are strong that we can help the weak. As you can see, wishing plays an important role, for we either allow ourselves to become what others will make of us, or we wish to become something better.

Did you ever toss a coin into a wishing well and make a wish? What if you had your own wishing well? Aware of it or not, that's precisely what we have. We have a personal genie within us. It is our subconscious. Its sole purpose is to serve us. It serves us by regulating our heart and breathing rate, body temperature, and the flow of hormones, just to name a few of its many functions. But another major function of the subconscious is to grant our every wish! And it works tirelessly, 24/7, granting us what it believes we want.
Adapted from: https://www.rotaryeclubone.org/makeups/articles/achievingyourwishe/
